title: Modifier key doesn't work when pressing multiple keys at the same time
author: hwooo

status.label: Awaiting current-build retest
status.detail: The reporter confirmed the issue on v0.73, but the latest visible question asks whether it persists on v0.100.2 or above and has no answer. PR #32125 was closed unmerged, so it is not evidence that a fix shipped.

next_action: Keep the existing current-version retest request open; do not treat closed, unmerged PR #32125 as a shipped fix.

judgment.rationale: The maintainer reproduced the simultaneous-key behavior on v0.37 and a reporter confirmed it still occurred on v0.73 with a video. A later comment asks whether it persists on v0.100.2 or above, but there is no response. The issue is assigned to gokcekantarci, who authored PR #32125, but that PR was closed without a merge commit; the report must not be marked fixed on that basis.
evidence: Issue #10393 is open and labeled Issue-Bug and Status-In progress; it is assigned to gokcekantarci and has ten comments.

The original report describes Alt+I/J/K/L remapped to cursor arrows and says that pressing Alt plus two action keys simultaneously can insert literal alphabetic characters instead of only moving the cursor.
A maintainer reproduced the behavior on PowerToys 0.37, and a reporter confirmed it on v0.73 with a screenshot and video.
On 2024-06-09, a commenter said the issue looked fixed by PR #32125. That PR explicitly references #10393 but was closed on 2025-03-28 with mergedAt and mergeCommit null.
The current assignee gokcekantarci authored PR #32125, so the issue already has an owner; no competing implementation should be started.
On 2026-07-28, Chealer asked whether the issue persists on v0.100.2 or above; no later reply is present. The 2026-10-11 issue update was label-only.
Current upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769 has shortcut invocation-state handling, but the issue-specific fix in closed PR #32125 is not proven to have shipped.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for the reporter to answer the current-build question; if the symptom persists, the assigned maintainer can revalidate the closed PR's approach against current main.

fix_assessment.rationale: A new competing fix proposal is not appropriate while the issue is assigned to the maintainer who authored its unmerged implementation attempt and the existing current-build retest request remains unanswered. This is a temporary ownership and evidence disposition, not a claim that the issue is fixed or that a code fix cannot apply.

issue_context.summary: When Alt is held and two mapped action keys are pressed simultaneously, Keyboard Manager can pass the literal letters into the editor instead of applying only the arrow remap.
known_information: The original report describes Alt+I/J/K/L mapped to cursor Up/Left/Down/Right and unintended alphabetic characters when two action keys are pressed at the same time.
A maintainer reproduced the issue on v0.37; a reporter later confirmed it still occurred on v0.73 and supplied a video.
A 2026-07-28 comment asks whether the behavior persists on v0.100.2 or above; the reporter has not answered.
The issue remains open, is assigned to gokcekantarci, and is labeled Status-In progress.
PR #32125 references #10393 and proposes simultaneous-shortcut changes, but is closed and unmerged.
inferences: The symptom may involve the handling of overlapping shortcut action-key events and whether an unmatched key-down leaks to the foreground application.
The closed PR may contain a useful implementation attempt, but its code cannot be treated as a shipped fix without a merge or current-build confirmation.
issue_context.analysis: This issue has strong historical reproduction evidence, but no current-version confirmation. The latest visible request already asks the reporter to retest on v0.100.2 or above, so another comment would duplicate the unanswered request. The issue is also assigned to the author of the related closed PR. Preserve the owner and wait for the requested confirmation; do not claim that PR #32125 fixed the issue.
